subject: Slab vs slope: per-token discount structure for HoloMed
messages:
From: Caroline Yu <caroline.yu@holomed.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing model question: per-token discount structure

Hi Connor,

Quick question as we scope the HoloMed pilot: we expect ~150M tokens / month once the models are in production, with an initial 12-month commitment. Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can do per-token marginal discounts (pure breakpoint/marginal pricing) versus a blended (effective) rate for billing stability.

Specifically:
- Can you show an example invoice under both approaches for 150M tokens?
- Do you support monthly true-ups or smoothing credits if actual usage is lumpy?
- Any minimums or floors we should be aware of?

Procurement wants a simple worked example they can share with finance. Can you send a short worked example + recommendation?

Thanks,
Caroline
Caroline Yu
Head of Product, HoloMed
caroline.yu@holomed.ai

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Yu <caroline.yu@holomed.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing model question: per-token discount structure

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass spreadsheet (HoloMed_commit_proposal_v1.xlsx) with two worked examples (marginal vs blended) and a sensitivity tab. High level:

- If we do pure marginal (breakpoints): you pay the listed incremental price on each tranche. This is simplest and tends to be lowest cost if you consistently run above breakpoints.
- If we invoice as blended (you see a single effective $/token on the invoice): we can offer smoothing so monthly invoices are more predictable; blended is easier for bookkeeping but typically yields a slightly higher effective unit price.
- We can do a middle ground: marginal pricing with a monthly "blending" view for finance plus a true-up that ensures both sides are within a committed floor/ceiling.

Example snapshot (from the attachment):
- 0–50M tokens: $0.00080 / token
- 50M–150M: $0.00060 / token (marginal)
- >150M: $0.00045 / token (marginal)

For 150M exactly: marginal invoice = (50M * 0.0008) + (100M * 0.0006) = effective blended $0.00065 / token.

Can we schedule a 30-min call (this week) to walk procurement through the examples and pick the invoicing style you prefer? I can loop in our pricing manager if you want to discuss smoothing/guardrails.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: HoloMed_commit_proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56KB)

Connor — quick thoughts:

- Start with marginal breakpoints that favor the customer early to demonstrate value (make 50M->150M jump meaningful).
- Offer blended invoice view as a sales convenience, but include a 6–12 month lookback true-up to protect Redwood.
- If they push on budget predictability, propose a small smoothing credit that phases out after month 3.

I'd keep the floor >= 60% of the list blended to protect margin. If procurement pushes, we can trade a slightly higher price at the top tranche for a longer commit length (18–24 months).

—Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Addendum to Marissa: negotiation play that has worked — propose marginal tiers but show a blended effective rate on the first invoice. Include an explicit monthly "smoothing" line item (credit up to X tokens) so finance sees a single number but we keep the marginal economics in the contract. If they want true blended pricing, require a 10% higher blended floor or longer commit.

Also recommend we document an example year-one invoice with the blended effective rate and attach it to the SOW so there is no confusion later.

—Ben

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing model question: per-token discount structure

Caroline — thanks for the patience while we dug in with pricing. Our recommended approach (attached memo) is the hybrid below. It preserves predictable invoices for Finance while keeping marginal economics for Redwood and you.

Hybrid proposal (12-month commit, monthly billing, month-end true-up):
- Marginal tiers (applied to usage):
  • 0–50M tokens: $0.00080 / token
  • 50M–150M: $0.00060 / token
  • >150M: $0.00045 / token

- Invoice presentation:
  • We will present a single blended effective $/token on the invoice for that month. Example: if usage = 150M, blended = $0.00065 / token (see worked example attached).
  • The underlying contract will record marginal tranches and a monthly true-up to reconcile billed blended vs marginal. If the blended invoice is higher than marginal due to smoothing, Redwood will apply a smoothing credit (up to a pre-agreed cap) to the following invoice.

- Protections & guardrails:
  • Floor guarantee: 60% of list blended (protects Redwood margin)
  • Smoothing cap: up to 10% of monthly invoice can be credited for volatility in first 3 months; then reviewed
  • Optional: 18-month commit for +10% discount on >150M tranche

- Why this helps HoloMed:
  • Finance gets a single-line blended invoice that is easy to budget for
  • Ops gets the lower marginal economics when traffic grows
  • We maintain an auditable true-up so both sides can see the math

Next steps: let me know if procurement prefers (A) pure marginal invoicing, (B) blended invoicing + true-up (our recommendation), or (C) fully blended pricing (requires additional concessions). If (B) we'll draft the SOW and attach the worked invoice example to the contract.

I've attached a short pricing memo that spells out examples and the mechanics. HubSpot link to the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/HLMD-2027-022

Connor O'Brien
